data.title: REG - Roebuck Food Group - Appointment of CEO and Executive Director
data.description:
RNS Number : 2791B Roebuck Food Group PLC 30 October 2026  

30 October 2026

ROEBUCK FOOD GROUP PLC

("Roebuck", the "Company" or the "Group", AIM: RFG)

Appointment of CEO and Executive Director

Roebuck Food Group plc (AIM: RFG), a group focused on growth and innovation within the food and agribusiness sectors, is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr Justin Gerard McCarthy as Chief Executive Officer and as an executive director of the Company, effective tomorrow 31 October 2026.

As announced in the Company’s interim results on 30 September 2026, Mr McCarthy succeeds Kieran Mahon following the refocusing of the Group’s business on its investments in Glasport Bio Limited (“GlasPort”) and Glasport Rumen Tech Limited (“Rumen Tech”).

Mr McCarthy (49) is currently Chief Executive Officer of GlasPort and Executive Chairman of Rumen Tech, roles he will retain following his appointment as CEO of Roebuck. Both businesses develop technologies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions from livestock production. He has experience across the agricultural sector, having worked with ABP Food Group, Dawn Meats and Teagasc, and previously served as CEO of the Irish Farmers Journal Group. He brings a combination of leadership, commercial insight and knowledge of agriculture and the global food sector. Mr McCarthy is a graduate in Agricultural Science from Harper Adams University and has also undertaken executive education at Harvard and University College Dublin’s Michael Smurfit Graduate Business School.

The following information in respect of Justin McCarthy is disclosed pursuant to Rule 17 of the AIM Rules for Companies:

Current directorships and directorships held in the last 5 years:

Glasport Bio Limited

Glasport Rumen Tech Limited

Tullamore Farm Limited

Current shareholdings of Roebuck, GlasPort and Rumen Tech:

Roebuck Food Group plc: 257,418 ordinary shares

Glasport Bio Limited: 30,653 ordinary A shares; 15,326 ordinary B shares; 15,326 ordinary C shares and 15,326 ordinary D shares

Glasport Rumen Tech Limited: 28,588 ordinary A shares; 14,294 ordinary B shares; 14,294 ordinary C shares and 14,294 ordinary D shares

Save as set out above, there is no additional information under Schedule 2, Part One, paragraph (g) of the AIM Rules for Companies which needs to be disclosed.

Commenting on his appointment, Mr McCarthy said:

“I am pleased to take on the role of Chief Executive of Roebuck Food Group at what is clearly an important point for the Group. There is a need to re-focus the business, establish a clear strategic direction and ensure that capital and management resources are deployed in the areas capable of delivering sustainable value for shareholders. The immediate priority will be to work with the team to build on the progress within GlasPort Bio and GlasPort Rumen Tech, accelerate the commercial development of our GasAbate technology and establish the disciplined platform required for the next phase of the Group’s development. I look forward to working with the Board, our shareholders and the wider team to build confidence and deliver long-term shareholder value.”

Commenting on the appointment of Mr McCarthy, Roebuck Chairman Tommy Conway stated:

“We are pleased to announce Justin McCarthy’s appointment as Chief Executive Officer of Roebuck as the Group refocuses its activities on its investments in GlasPort and Rumen Tech. GlasPort continues to progress, with GasAbate installations on commercial dairy farms across Ireland, Northern Ireland and Continental Europe, growing interest from farmers and processors, and development of the next version of its Compli360 dosage and verification platform. The Group is encouraged by the solid operational and commercial progress to date and is confident that the business will continue to develop under Mr McCarthy’s stewardship.”

The directors of the Company accept responsibility for this announcement.

data.title: Delhivery Q2 Results: Revenue crosses ₹3,000 crore for first time; EBITDA nearly triples
data.description:
Delhivery Ltd on Friday (October 30) reported its first-ever quarterly revenue of over ₹3,000 crore, with revenue from services rising 20% year-on-year to ₹3,066 crore in the second quarter of FY27.

EBITDA nearly tripled year-on-year to ₹205 crore, with a margin of 6.7%, while consolidated net profit stood at ₹41 crore, or a margin of 1.3%.

The company's express parcel business handled 325 million shipments during the quarter, up 32% year-on-year, while revenue from the segment grew 22%. Part Truck Load (PTL) volumes rose 14% to 545,000 metric tonnes (MT), with revenue increasing 23% year-on-year.

Delhivery ended the September quarter with a cash balance of ₹4,676 crore.

The company said its profitability improved sequentially despite an inflationary cost environment. It also reported its best network service levels ahead of the festive season, despite rising fuel prices, labour availability issues and multiple statutory changes.

Delhivery said it continues to invest in technology to improve demand shaping, infrastructure productivity, reduce dependence on labour in under-the-roof operations and simplify customer experience.

The company said its early investments in artificial intelligence (AI) are beginning to deliver results through improved sales productivity and customer onboarding, faster resolution of claims and disputes, and fraud detection.

Delhivery Robotics, its in-house automation lab, has started production of customised autonomous vehicles for in-facility movement operations. The company has also begun testing robotics systems across under-the-roof operations in partnership with global leaders in the physical AI domain.

Delhivery said the improvements in network service levels and profitability provide momentum heading into the second half of FY27.

The company serves over 59,000 clients across e-commerce and express parcel transportation, PTL and full truckload (FTL) freight, warehousing and supply chain solutions, international freight, intra-city on-demand logistics, data solutions and software-as-a-service offerings, including AI-powered mapping APIs and warehouse and transportation management systems.

data.title: Caterpillar, Deere on Different Roads With Investors Lately — WSJ
data.description:
By Bob Tita

Caterpillar's strong generator business with AI data centers made it the envy of the machinery industry over the last year as the company's shares soared with high-flying tech stocks.

But decent third-quarter sales and profit from the construction and mining equipment maker on Thursday were brushed aside by jittery investors. The company's shares dropped more than 9% Thursday in a sell-off of stocks with exposure to the AI sector. Caterpillar, which has fallen more than 20% in the past month, was down about 4% Friday.

Rival machinery manufacturer Deere, which ironically has for years tried to attract more tech-focused investors with its automated farming software, has avoided the AI carnage. Deere's shares are up about 45% since the start of the year. Investors have piled into Deere on the expectation that a long slump in the U.S. farm equipment market will ease next year and farmers will start buying more Deere tractors again.

Deere is up about 1.5% on Friday.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Fed Needs to Implement at Least Two More Rate Increases, Dallas Fed's Logan Says — Update
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

The Federal Reserve needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases given the current economic outlook after the central bank voted to hold interest rates steady this week, according to Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan.

Without any monetary-policy restraint, inflation will continue to trend above target unless unexpected shocks occur, Logan said at an event in Davidson, N.C., on Friday.

"It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases," Logan said. "After that, it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate," she added.

There had been speculation that Logan would dissent at October's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, given her previous calls for tighter monetary policy and a previous dissent she gave in July. On Friday, she offered more explanation to why she instead supported the committee's decision to hold interest rates where they are.

Financial markets have been volatile in response to news on the technology-investment outlook and geopolitical developments, she said. In such an environment, adjusting policy more gradually can help households, businesses and market participants adapt to higher rates and reduce the risk that economic activity deteriorates more sharply than necessary, she added.

Moreover, Logan said the precise timing of each rate increase has little effect on the longer-term rates most borrowers pay as long as market participants understand the FOMC's policy plans.

In addition, skipping a meeting of rate increases doesn't change the monetary-policy destination, Logan argued.

"By making the destination clear, the FOMC can better help the economy adapt and obtain the promised benefits of a skip," she explained.

Given the current outlook, the end goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive to sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices, Logan said.

Write to Jessica Coacci at jessica.coacci@wsj.com

data.title: Bank of Canada Must Rethink Further Rate Hikes Amid 'Squishy-Soft' Data — Market Talk
data.description: Days after raising its policy rate by a quarter point, the Bank of Canada faces a reality check over its outlook for accelerating growth, says David Rosenberg, head of market-strategy firm Rosenberg Research. Data covering non-farm payrolls indicate a 49,600 decline in jobs in August. Further, GDP stalled in August, and is expected to contract in September--leading to annualized growth of 1.3% in 3Q, or well below the BOC's 2% forecast. "Can the central bank really ignore the economy and this recent squishy-soft set of economic data?," says Rosenberg about pending rate hikes. He argues BOC based its rate-hike decision on "dubious surveys instead of facts on the ground," adding there is no evidence of elevated fuel prices spilling over to non-energy goods. (paul.vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)

data.title: AMD Stocks Drop 11% With a $13 Billion Revenue Test Approaching
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices , the processor and AI-accelerator designer, has a bigger hurdle than winning server business: turning that growth into profit. Shares fell 11.01% to $504.05 at 12:45 p.m. ET on October 30, ahead of its November 3 earnings report. Susquehanna raised its price target from $620 to $650 and maintained Buy, pointing to data-center opportunities while flagging margin pressure from the GPU ramp. That leaves investors weighing a bigger sales opportunity against the cost of delivering it.

The numbers give that debate a clear test. AMD's August outlook called for September-quarter revenue of $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, with adjusted gross margin near 56%. The revenue midpoint implies roughly 12.7% growth from the June quarter's $11.536 billion. More revenue could strengthen the AI story, but holding margins while expanding GPU deliveries would provide firmer evidence that the opportunity is translating into profitable growth.

GuruFocus' snapshot captures the tension: an 82/100 GF Score, strong growth and financial-strength readings, but a weak GF Value reading. At 129.34 times earnings and 12.24 times book value, the valuation appears to leave limited room for disappointment even after the sharp decline. Susquehanna's roughly 4.8% target increase adds optimism; November's results must supply the evidence. Revenue delivery, gross margin and the next outlook could determine whether AMD's expanding data-center business can support those expectations.
